This same secretaire bookcase was UNSOLD twice at Gowans in October (5 and 4 bids, last bids not shown). The top of the range is a single dealer ASKING price of $1,795 for a restored piece. lots.working: No same-item SOLD exists: this exact piece passed in twice. The maximum bids rest on close Gowans SOLD sales of plain 19th c. glazed bookcases. A secretaire is the more desirable form, so these are conservative. Keep: lowest close SOLD $320 (Sep 2026) / 1.198 = $267.11, rounded down to $265 (all-in about $317). Flip: likely resale $420 (best close Gowans hammer, Oct 2026), less a 15% vendor commission ($63) and $0 outbound postage (buyer collects) = $357, / 2.396 = $149, rounded down to $145. A flip is not realistic, because the vendor's reserve has twice sat above the room. Even the keep bid will only win if the reserve has been lowered for this third run.
lots.confidence_reason: The title, dimensions and photo agree, and there are three close Gowans SOLD results with the pages opened. None of them is the same form, and the reserve is unknown.

lots.guide_summary: No same-item or close entry survives verification. The only close entry (Bonhams, US$1,000) is a snippet-only lead. The category guides run from Gowans mixed-lot SOLD hammers of $40 and $75, through a 2021 US sale of A$179 and a UK pass-in on an estimate of about A$573 to A$954, to a Leonard Joel estimate of A$300 to A$500 for a single good Dr Wall teapot. Rates: US$1 = A$1.4286, GBP 1 = A$1.909.
lots.working: There is no same-item SOLD within 24 months. The Gowans SOLD results ($40 and $75) are mixed lots of different content, and the Potomack sale is from 2021 and partly reproductions. So keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. If the teapot and the crescent-marked pieces are confirmed as genuine 18th century Worcester or Caughley at the viewing, the box could be worth several hundred dollars to a specialist buyer. That is a judgement, not sold evidence.
lots.confidence_reason: The marks are read, but a crescent and a pseudo-script mark do not prove the factory (Caughley, Samson and later copies all used them). The damage is not assessed, and no comparable sold evidence exists.
lots.dropped_entries: Bonhams Oxford 17079 lot 397 (GBP 384, 2009) dropped: snippet only, the page returned 403, it is 17 years old, and it is a single dish. The researcher's Gowans single-lot URLs (/backend/api/v1/lots/390812) do not return the record (HTTP 301); I replaced them with the working search URLs. The Potomack price, date (25 Mar 2021) and estimate are now confirmed from the opened page, and I corrected the rates to live ones.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged, the cup base shows a small hand-painted blue open crescent, a Worcester mark also used by Caughley and copyists. The pierced strainer base shows a blue script or pseudo-monogram mark, possibly a disguised numeral or workman's mark, and a clear crack running from the rim into the base. The teapot is fluted with a blue-scale shoulder, gilt scale outlines and a floral panel. Its lid is Imari or Kakiemon-style polychrome with a green flower knop, which may be a replacement or marriage. The blue and white pieces carry chinoiserie landscape, floral and pagoda patterns typical of Worcester and Caughley transfer and painted wares. A brown discolouration and wear show on the sauceboat.
lots.condition: Some damage, as stated. A crack is visible on the strainer. Other chips, hairlines and restorations are unseen, and the teapot lid may not be original.
lots.question_for_gowans: Can you list the damage piece by piece, especially the teapot (spout, lid, handle) and the large sauceboat? Is the teapot lid original to it? Are any other pieces marked (crescent, 'S', 'C' or a square seal)? Is there any vendor provenance or attribution?
